title: North Rauceby T.2834 Memorial

external_narratives.summary: Detailed account of the loss of Wellington T2834 from No. 3 Coastal Operational Training Unit at RAF Cranwell on 20 April 1942. P/O Henry Eric Rath (J/6686 RCAF, age 21) and Sgt Karl Morris Miegel (AUS/403480 RAAF, age 27) were conducting night circuit and landing practice when the aircraft flew into high ground near the vicarage at North Rauceby at 0120 hours.
key_details: Rath buried in Cranwell Churchyard (St Andrew), Plot 3 Row E Grave 1

narrative: Wellington T.2834 was on a training flight from RAF Cranwell when it came down near North Rauceby, Lincolnshire, on 20 April 1942. The aircraft, assigned to 3 OTU, was under the command of Pilot Officer Henry Eric Rath, aged 21. The crash was recorded as a training accident, though no specific cause is documented. Five of the six crew members were killed: Pilot Officer Rath, Sergeant Ernest A. Hoagg, Sergeant John H. Lewis, Sergeant Walter Gavin, and Sergeant Leslie J. Hill. The outcome for the sixth crew member, Sergeant Douglas J. Roberts, remains unknown. Sergeant John H. Lewis, the observer, was 31 — the eldest among the crew members whose ages are recorded.
